draft.why_angle: The cited pages list 58.4 V and amp ratings, but none compares a charger's output with what a household circuit can carry continuously. This page shows that the 30 A fast-charge pick needs 1,536–1,752 W, while a 15 A, 120 V circuit allows 1,440 W. It also puts every candidate's output power, published wall draw and constant-current hours side by side.

page.desc: Redodo 58.4V 18A is our pick for a 48V lithium golf cart: 1,051 W fits a 15 A outlet's 1,440 W continuous limit, and 100Ah charges in 5.6 h. Here's why 30A units don't.
page.answer: Short answer. The best 48V lithium golf cart charger for most 58.4V LiFePO4 packs is the Redodo 58.4V 18A: 1,051 W stays under a 15 A garage outlet's 1,440 W continuous limit and refills 100Ah in 5.6 h. A 30A charger needs up to 1,752 W; the Lester Summit II 650W tops out at 13.5 A.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • The outlet limit. Under the NEC, a load that runs at full current for 3 hours or more is continuous, and the breaker must cover 125% of it. That leaves 80% of the breaker for the load: 15 A × 120 V × 0.8 = 1,440 W (12 A).
  • 18 A chargers. 58.4 V × 18 A = 1,051 W at the very end of the charge, which leaves headroom on a shared 15 A circuit. 100 Ah ÷ 18 A = 5.6 h of constant current, which matches the 5.6 h Redodo quotes for its own 48V 100Ah kit.
  • LiTime 30A. 51.2 V × 30 A = 1,536 W and 58.4 V × 30 A = 1,752 W. Both are above 1,440 W before conversion loss is added, and 100 Ah ÷ 30 A = 3.3 h, which is past the 3-hour mark for a continuous load.
  • Vatrer 20A. Vatrer lists a 13 A maximum AC input, which is above the 12 A continuous figure for a 15 A circuit (15 × 0.8).
  • Lester Summit II 650W. 650 W ÷ 58.4 V = 11.1 A near full charge. Per amp it costs $409 ÷ 13.5 A = $30.30/A, against $149.99 ÷ 18 A = $8.33/A for the Redodo.

Converting with a Redodo 48V 100Ah or Vatrer 48V 105Ah kitAlready in the box: both kits include a 58.4 V 18 A charger

Will it run on your garage outlet?

A lithium charger spends most of its cycle in the constant-current stage, drawing close to its full power for hours. The wall has to supply that output plus conversion loss, so DC output is the lowest the wall draw can be. Here is what each maker publishes for the input side:

ChargerPeak DC outputAC input, as published
Redodo 58.4V 18A1,051 W100–240 V AC, 47–63 Hz
LiTime 18A1,051 W100–240 V AC
LiTime 30A1,752 W100–240 V AC
Vatrer 20A1,160 W100–240 V nominal, 13 A maximum
Lester Summit II 650W650 W100–240 V AC, under 8 A; over 90% peak efficiency at 115 V

All five accept 240 V input. On a 240 V circuit the LiTime 30A's 1,752 W works out to about 7.3 A before losses (1,752 ÷ 240), so it is a reasonable fast charger in a garage wired that way. On a shared 15 A, 120 V outlet, an 18 A unit is the fastest charger in this group that stays under the continuous limit. The Redodo costs the least of those and wakes a pack whose BMS has shut off (0 V activation): {buy:redodo-58-4v-18a-lifepo4-charger}. If you are still choosing a battery, the {buy:redodo-48v-100ah-golf-cart-conversion-kit} and the {buy:vatrer-48v-105ah-club-car-golf-cart-battery-kit} both include a charger (Vatrer's ICON and EZGO kit listings name it as 58.4 V 18 A).

The Lester works differently. Lester's FAQ says the Summit II charges lithium on its standard wet-cell (IEI) profiles, with the battery's own controller capping the voltage, and that its chargers need about 15 VDC at the terminals to start. That suits a cart whose lithium pack talks to the charger. It does not suit a generic drop-in pack whose BMS has disconnected after a deep discharge. Golf Cart Lab sells the 650W with a Club Car 3-pin cord at $690 and a 48-month Lester warranty.

Not recommended

LiTime 30A on a shared 15 A outlet. Its 1,536–1,752 W output is already above the 1,440 W continuous figure before any conversion loss, and it holds that load for more than 3 hours on a 100 Ah pack. LiTime also recommends it for indoor use. Buy it only for a dedicated 20 A or 240 V circuit. Vatrer E15-58.4V20A for now. Vatrer lists it as a pre-order, its program ends in a float stage, and its 13 A maximum input is above 12 A on a 15 A circuit.
